question.problem: Given that $Q(1,-3,7)$ lies on the plane $Π:r\cdot ⟨6,3,-2⟩=-17$, find the shortest distance from $P(2,-6,2)$ to $Π.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨1,-3,7⟩-⟨2,-6,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,3,5⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨6,3,-2⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-1)\cdot 6+3\cdot 3+5\cdot (-2)|}{\sqrt{{6}^{2}+{3}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-6+9-10|}{\sqrt{36+9+4}} \\  & =\frac{|-7|}{\sqrt{49}} \\  & =\frac{7}{7} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
